resources.string: How big each random step of the noise is. Higher values make the sound rougher, closer to white noise, lower values make it calmer and deeper.
How strongly the noise is initially smoothed while being generated. Higher values make it softer, darker and deeper; lower values keep more detail and brightness.
How different the left and right channels are. 0% means mono, 100% makes the sound wide and enveloping.
Additional filtering where frequencies above this value are cut off. Lower values make the sound even more deep and muffled

Shape of the cutoff. Low values give a crisp cutoff right at the chosen frequency; high values stretch it out so it starts much lower, making the sound softer and more muffled. 0% turns the filter off.
Output level, not available while Auto-normalize is on (constant -8 dB).
